issues.reason: The verb_particle rule is not the only licence: Compound concepts also licenses a fixed multi-word idiom as 'the single surface symbol, keeping every word' with no genus (spill_the_beans), and unpacking the euphemism into a literal sleep event is exactly what that rule forbids — the reused 'with' leaves no atom false, ill-typed or over-asserted, since the symbol is opaque and Bergin really is a co-participant.

The role mismatch stands — Experiencer is reserved for stative psych/property predication while CoAgent is defined as a second doer, so the volitional idiom reading takes Agent ('when unclear, Agent') — but the progressive half does not: the instruction set reifies progressive statives with an Experiencer subject ('was lying across the threshold'), so 'was sleeping' argues nothing either way.

gaps_confirmed: a prepositional verb with an idiomatic sense whose preposition is also a comitative role marker ('sleep with X', 'go out with X') — verb_particle fusion, the fixed-idiom rule and the prepositional-verb oblique each cover part of it and give different answers, and none says which slot the object NP takes
new_gaps: the idiom coherence test ('take the idiomatic reading only when the literal one is incoherent for these participants') misfires on a euphemism whose literal reading stays coherent but is plainly not meant, as here

a non-compositional adjective+noun idiom ('a screaming match') — the compound-kind rule forces a genus (Inheritance screaming_match match) that the idiom does not support, while the no-genus idiom treatment is written for multi-word verb idioms
repair_summary: Changed the sealed (Experiencer sk_sleep_with_1 carolyn) to (Agent sk_sleep_with_1 carolyn), so the subject role matches the CoAgent co-participant it is paired with; nothing else, including the sleep_with symbol and the Still/Ongoing/Past atoms, is touched.
notes: The frame is otherwise right: During over both reified eventualities, Year on the event-noun with no tense of its own, the non-factive seal under tell's Theme, and Bergin's Name projected outside it.
